# Story 19 — Email & Web Forms Communication Channels

## Prerequisites

- Story 07–09 completed: `Customer` and `CustomerInteraction` domain models available under `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Domain/Customers/`.
- Story 10–14 completed: Ticket model, service, history under `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Tickets/` and `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Domain/Tickets/`.
- Story 15 completed: Agent Dashboard consumes Tickets via existing endpoints.
- Story 17 completed: Quick Replies template CRUD and `QuickReplyPicker` (`frontend/src/features/quick-replies/QuickReplyPicker.tsx`). This story only **consumes** the picker.
- Story 18 completed: internal collaboration comments do not interfere with customer-facing interactions.
- Coordinate with owner of `CrmDbContext` / migrations before adding new tables (`OutboundEmailMessage`, `InboundEmailMessage`) and new `CustomerInteraction` channel values.

---

## Story Goal

Add Email (inbound + outbound) and Web Form (inbound only) as first-class communication channels that feed the **existing** Ticket workflow. Customers who email `support@…` or submit the public Web Form must:

1. Be matched to an existing `Customer` by normalized email, or created if none exists.
2. Get a Ticket created (or an existing Ticket updated when the inbound email can be reliably matched to a prior conversation).
3. Have the raw message persisted as a `CustomerInteraction` with `InteractionType = "Email"` or `"WebForm"`.

Agents opening an Email-created Ticket can compose a reply, insert Story 17 Quick Replies, edit, and **explicitly** press Send. Sending calls an `IEmailSender` abstraction; on success the reply is persisted as an outbound `CustomerInteraction` on the same Ticket.

**Not in scope:** automatic assignment (Story 23), WhatsApp/SMS (Story 20), Live Chat (Story 21), SLA (Stories 22–25), AI (Stories 39–43), customer portal (Stories 29–33).

### 1 — New domain entities for raw communication payloads

Create file: `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Domain/Communications/InboundEmailMessage.cs`

```csharp
namespace CustomerSupportCrm.Domain.Communications;

/// <summary>
/// Story 19 — raw inbound email payload, preserved verbatim for audit.
/// Business linking (customer, ticket, interaction) is done by the application layer.
/// </summary>
public class InboundEmailMessage
{
    public Guid Id { get; set; } = Guid.NewGuid();
    public string MessageId { get; set; } = string.Empty;   // RFC 5322 Message-Id, unique
    public string? InReplyTo { get; set; }                  // RFC 5322 In-Reply-To
    public string? References { get; set; }                 // RFC 5322 References
    public string FromAddress { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    public string? FromName { get; set; }
    public string ToAddress { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    public string Subject { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    public string BodyText { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    public string? BodyHtml { get; set; }
    public DateTime ReceivedAt { get; set; } = DateTime.UtcNow;

    public Guid? CustomerId { get; set; }
    public Guid? TicketId { get; set; }
    public Guid? CustomerInteractionId { get; set; }
}
```

### 4 — Email abstractions (application layer)

Create folder: `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Communications/Email/`

Files:

- `IEmailSender.cs`
  ```csharp
  public interface IEmailSender
  {
      Task<EmailSendResult> SendAsync(OutboundEmail message, CancellationToken ct = default);
  }
  public record OutboundEmail(string To, string Subject, string BodyText, string? InReplyTo, string? References);
  public record EmailSendResult(bool Success, string? ProviderMessageId, string? Error);
  ```
- `EmailOptions.cs` — bound from `appsettings.json` section `"Email"`: `FromAddress`, `FromName`, `SmtpHost`, `SmtpPort`, `Username`, `Password`, `UseSsl`, `WebhookSecret`.
- `SmtpEmailSender.cs` — default `IEmailSender`; if `EmailOptions.SmtpHost` is empty, register a `NullEmailSender` that logs and returns `Success = false` so unit/dev environments do not silently drop mail.
- `IInboundEmailProcessor.cs` and `InboundEmailProcessor.cs` — receives a `RawInboundEmail(fromAddress, fromName, toAddress, subject, bodyText, bodyHtml, messageId, inReplyTo, references, receivedAt)` and orchestrates:
  1. Persist `InboundEmailMessage` row (transaction start).
  2. Reject duplicate `MessageId` (idempotency) — return without creating anything else.
  3. Normalize `fromAddress` via `EmailNormalizer` → look up `Customer`; if not found, create via `CustomersService.FindOrCreateByEmailAsync`.
  4. Resolve target ticket:
     - Extract ticket reference from `Subject` matching regex `\[#(?<code>[A-Za-z0-9-]+)\]` (Ticket reference token — see Story 10 code, grep for existing `TicketNumber` / `Code` field).
     - Else, look up the `InboundEmailMessage.MessageId` referenced by `InReplyTo` / `References`; if that inbound row is linked to a Ticket that is not `Closed`, reuse it.
     - Else, call `TicketsService` to create a new Ticket (`CustomerId`, `Subject`, `Description = BodyText`, default status/priority).
  5. Create one `CustomerInteraction` with `InteractionType = InteractionChannels.Email`, `Summary = subject`, `Details = bodyText`, `OccurredAt = receivedAt`, `CustomerId`, `UserId = null`.
  6. Backfill `InboundEmailMessage.CustomerId/TicketId/CustomerInteractionId`. Commit transaction.
- `InboundEmailController.cs` — POST `/api/communications/email/inbound`; **authorized via `WebhookSecret` header** (not JWT) so an email-provider webhook can call it. Body is `RawInboundEmail`. Delegates to `IInboundEmailProcessor`. Returns `202 Accepted`.

### 5 — Outbound reply endpoint

Create file: `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Communications/Email/OutboundEmailController.cs`

- `POST /api/tickets/{ticketId:guid}/replies/email` — body `{ subject, bodyText }`.
- `[HasPermission(Permissions.Communications.EmailSend)]` (see task 8).
- Loads Ticket + Customer; rejects if `Customer.Email` is null/empty (`400`).
- Creates `OutboundEmailMessage` row with `Status = Pending`.
- Calls `IEmailSender.SendAsync` with `InReplyTo` set to the most recent `InboundEmailMessage.MessageId` on the ticket (query top 1 by `ReceivedAt desc`), so the thread stays intact in the customer's mailbox.
- If `EmailSendResult.Success`:
  - Set `Status = Sent`, `SentAt = UtcNow`, `MessageId = result.ProviderMessageId`.
  - Create `CustomerInteraction` with `InteractionType = InteractionChannels.Email`, `Summary = "Reply: {subject}"`, `Details = bodyText`, `UserId = current agent`.
  - Persist link `OutboundEmailMessage.CustomerInteractionId`.
  - Return `200` with DTO.
- If **not** success:
  - Set `Status = Failed`, `ProviderError = result.Error`. **Do not** create a `CustomerInteraction`.
  - Return `502 Bad Gateway` with a problem detail so the UI can surface "delivery failed".
- Whole operation wrapped in a `IDbContextTransaction`.

Never mutate `Ticket.Status` here (Story 13 owns transitions).

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Duplicate inbound email (same `Message-Id`)** → `InboundEmailProcessor` short-circuits after the unique-index insert throws; no second Ticket/Interaction created. Enforced by unique index in migration (task 2) and try/catch in `InboundEmailProcessor.cs`.
- **Concurrent inbound emails from the same brand-new customer** → race on `Customers.Email` unique index; caught in `FindOrCreateByEmailAsync` (task 7) which retries the lookup.
- **Reply-to a ticket that is `Closed`** → treat as a new Ticket (do not silently reopen — Story 13 owns state).
- **Customer without email address** on outbound → `OutboundEmailController` returns `400` before touching provider.
- **SMTP provider transient failure** → `OutboundEmailMessage.Status = Failed`, no `CustomerInteraction`, `502` surfaced to UI. Retry is manual (out of scope; note in code comment for a future retry story).
- **Web Form spam burst** → rate-limiter `"web-form"` returns `429`; captcha rejection returns `400`.
- **Invalid inbound webhook secret** → `401`. Do not reveal whether the shared secret exists.
- **Unicode in subject / body** → all string columns are `nvarchar`; `SmtpEmailSender` uses UTF-8 encoding. Verify test covers Arabic subject `"طلب دعم"`.
- **HTML-only inbound email** (`BodyText` empty) → store as-is; `Description` on the ticket falls back to a stripped-tags version so the ticket is readable.
- **Ticket reference token spoofing** (customer types `[#OTHER-123]` in subject to hijack a ticket) → after regex extraction, additionally verify the resolved Ticket's `CustomerId` matches the resolved inbound customer; if not, ignore the token and create a new Ticket.

## Migration / Rollback

- **Forward:** `dotnet ef database update --project backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Infrastructure --startup-project backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api`. New tables `InboundEmailMessages`, `OutboundEmailMessages`; new unique index on `InboundEmailMessages.MessageId`.
- **Rollback:** `dotnet ef database update <PreviousMigration> …`. Drops both tables. **Half-applied risk:** if only `InboundEmailMessages` is present, the API will still boot but outbound send throws on save — mitigated because both DbSets are added in the same migration.
- **Permissions:** `DbSeeder` is idempotent (existing pattern); re-running the API grants `communications.email.send` to seeded Agent/Manager roles without duplicating rows.
- **Config rollback:** removing the `Email` section in `appsettings.json` degrades to `NullEmailSender`; the API still starts and outbound returns `502`.
